paper.title: Structurally Aligned Subtask-Level Memory for Software Engineering Agents
paper.central_claim: Aligning storage, retrieval and online updates with functional SWE subtasks mitigates instance-memory interference and improves Pass@1 by 4.7 pp on average across four backbones, especially for long-horizon tasks.

provenance.notes: Dispatched agent_model=sonnet; configured upstream gpt-6.1-sol per task; no independently accessible model receipt or stable session identifier; no probing.

sections_read: entire supplied HTML text, no separate appendix present

evidence.quote: Integrating transition logic directly into the system prompt allows the agent to autonomously monitor its progress.
evidence.support_explanation: Agent predicts stage changes and localized intents; no separate trained segmenter.

evidence.quote: This explicit partitioning drastically reduces the candidate pool, enforcing structural alignment, ensuring that the agent only accesses experiences within the same functional scope (e.g., excluding debugging heuristics during a code-editing phase).
evidence.support_explanation: Category filter precedes top-1 intent embedding match, rather than global issue matching.

Crucially, for our method, the per-instance step limit encompasses both the agent’s reasoning steps and the memory extraction overhead, ensuring a budget-neutral comparison.
evidence.support_explanation: Memory overhead included in step cap; not full dollar/token accounting.

evidence.quote: All experiments follow a test-time streaming protocol: the memory storage
evidence.support_explanation: Memory built on evaluation stream, not a frozen independently constructed store.

evidence.quote: To mitigate ordering effects inherent to streaming, we perform three independent runs, using distinct random seeds to shuffle the execution sequence of the 500 instances, and report Avg. Pass@1 as mean
evidence.support_explanation: Three shuffled streams with mean/std, no significance or confidence interval.

evidence.quote: Across all four backbones, our method improves Pass@1 by +4.7 pp on average.
evidence.support_explanation: Four models; means in Table 1 improve 5.6/6.8/3.9/2.3 pp over vanilla.

evidence.quote: In this setting, the agent is explicitly prompted to adhere to the structured workflow and autonomously determine subtask transitions, yet operates without any memory retrieval or update mechanisms.
evidence.support_explanation: Structure-only control isolates memory beyond prompting; 53.2 vs 56.1 full and 52.2 vanilla.

evidence.quote: In this baseline, the retrieval mechanism performs a global search across the entire collection of accumulated memories to select the top-1 experience based on similarity, bypassing the category-specific constraint utilized in our full method.
evidence.support_explanation: Category-off 53.8 vs 56.1; raw-trajectory 53.4 distinguishes routing and abstraction.

evidence.quote: In the initial buckets (Instances 1-200), the memory state is sparse; the agent exhibits a slight performance dip
evidence.support_explanation: Reported early harm and one-run growth diagnostic; not proof of held-out transfer.

evidence.quote: Our work differs by (i) shifting the memory unit to fine-grained experience, and (ii) updating memory online by abstracting actionable experiences from completed subtasks, directly addressing the granularity mismatch between episodic memory and stage-structured reasoning in SWE agents.
evidence.support_explanation: Specific nearest-neighbor delta, as described by authors, not independently audited prior art.

signatures.object: Persistent subtask-experience triples and retrieval index
signatures.information: Current issue/codebase/history and subtask-intent; same-backbone execution correctness judgment, not benchmark answer labels.
signatures.operation: Predict Analyze/Reproduce/Edit/Verify intent; category-filter then top-1 cosine retrieve; inject experience; extract de-instantiated success/failure insight and append triple after subtask.
signatures.output: Growing non-weight memory and augmented future subtask context
signatures.conditions: Task admits meaningful stages; predicted category and embedding relevance reliable.
signatures.feedback: Subtask traces plus LLM correctness judgment
signatures.selection_rule: Append extracted entry; top-1 category-constrained retrieval, no measured admission gate.
signatures.selection_data: Previously completed subtasks within shuffled 500-task stream
signatures.persistence: External S_sub repository across subtasks and subsequent issues; initialized empty per independent run.
signatures.later_use: Injected at initialization of subsequent matching subtasks.
signatures.claimed_effect: Four-backbone mean +4.7 pp; Claude 3.7 56.1 vs 52.2 vanilla.
signatures.failure_boundary: Early sparse-memory dip; erroneous memories and hard misclassification untested; no deletion/rollback.

gap.author_gap: Instance/global issue similarity cannot represent stage-dependent reasoning requirements.
gap.checked_gap: Table 3 category-off and Table 4 raw memory support a local-granularity bottleneck, not a general failure of all instance-memory methods.

gap.stakes: Irrelevant memory can degrade even capable Claude backbones.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported online stream SWE gains and component ablations; independent construction/evaluation separation absent, so no retained certification under EVIDENCE rule 2.

G.reason: Specific global-vs-local granularity mismatch and ReasoningBank comparison; adjacent papers are only characterized within this source, not independently fixed.

M.reason: Stage-intent triple, same-backbone extractor, category then similarity retrieval directly target interference; correctness proxy and hard-category errors remain unvalidated.

X.reason: Read/write/transition chain reconstructible; append-only writes lack measured gate, deduplication, retirement and no-match fallback.

E.measurement.reason: 500 executable SWE-bench Verified patches and mean Pass@1, with best-of-three explicitly distinguished; no independent verifier audit.

E.causality.reason: Same scaffold plus structure-only, category-off and raw-history controls strongly isolate mechanism on one model; full token-matched alternate optimizer absent.

E.holdout.reason: Online shuffled benchmark stream reports later-task use but construction/evaluation not disjoint; no frozen-store external test or overlap audit.

E.statistics.reason: Three independently shuffled streams, means/std and early negative bins; lacks CIs/significance for full method and ablations.

E.cost.reason: Step cap includes extraction and same backbone; total tokens/dollars, embedding/storage growth and extraction overhead breakdown absent.
